title: An Account of the Manners and Customs of the Modern Egyptians
author: Edward William Lane
notes: Project Gutenberg #70796; complete with transcriber's corrections list. First edition 1836 (Gutenberg text is a later standard edition of the same work). Covers domestic life, law, religion, customs. Second Afro-Asiatic entry alongside the Rwala Bedouin.

title: Tsuni-||Goam: The Supreme Being of the Khoi-Khoi
author: Theophilus Hahn
notes: Google scan; complete to 'THE END' and printer's imprint; OCR readable. Flag: centred on religion and mythology with comparative-philological argument, less on kinship and law; no fuller English monograph found online (Kolben 1731 English translation not located on IA or Gutenberg). Avoid the noisier copy tsuni-goam-the-supreme-being-of-the-khoi-khoi-theophilus-hahn.

title: The Angami Nagas, with Some Notes on Neighbouring Tribes
author: J. H. Hutton
notes: Complete with index and printer's imprint; OCR readable.

title: The Mundas and Their Country
author: Sarat Chandra Roy
notes: Digital Library of India scan; complete from title page through final appendix; OCR readable. Large historical section precedes the ethnographic chapters.

title: The Euahlayi Tribe: A Study of Aboriginal Life in Australia
author: K. Langloh Parker
notes: Project Gutenberg #3819; complete through the glossary, Gutenberg end marker. IA Google scan also complete (~59k tokens incl. index): https://archive.org/download/euahlayitribewi00langgoog/euahlayitribewi00langgoog_djvu.txt.

title: Calendar History of the Kiowa Indians (17th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, Part 1, pp. 129-444)
author: James Mooney
notes: Project Gutenberg #46479; complete through index and Gutenberg end marker. Flag: weak fit, mainly tribal history and the pictographic calendars, with shorter sections on social organisation, the Sun Dance and customs; kept because no other pre-1929 Kiowa-Tanoan monograph was found online (Parsons 1925 Jemez and 1929 Tewa not located / too late).

title: The Seri Indians (17th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, Part 1)
author: W J McGee (with J. N. B. Hewitt, Comparative Lexicology of Seri)
notes: Google scan of Part 1 of the report; complete through Hewitt's lexicology appendix; OCR readable.

title: The Russian Peasantry: Their Agrarian Condition, Social Life, and Religion
author: Stepniak (S. M. Kravchinsky)
notes: Google scan; complete with index; OCR readable. Flag: a social and political study by a Russian emigre rather than fieldwork ethnography, but covers the village commune, family, customs and religion/sects. Included for European coverage in place of Robertson's Kafirs of the Hindu-Kush (Indo-European limit of 2).

title: Ethnology of the Yuchi Indians (Anthropological Publications of the University Museum, University of Pennsylvania, vol. 1, no. 1)
author: Frank G. Speck
notes: Complete through the plates; OCR readable. Avoid ethnologyofyuchi00specuoft (bound with other papers, ~180k words).
